note: Dimensions of a market configuration. A rule belongs to one pole of one dimension. A profile is a configuration: one pole per dimension, or nothing (keep the page as it is). Tendencies observed in the cited studies, never universal truths about people. `measures` lists the page metrics that describe a dimension (our own approximate operationalisation); an empty list means no metric describes it yet.

dimensions.name: Information density
dimensions.description: How much content a page packs per screen.

poles.name: Spacious
poles.description: Fewer items per screen, more room around them.

poles.name: Compact
poles.description: More items per screen, tighter layout.

dimensions.name: Spacing scale
dimensions.description: Space between blocks and around headers and footers.

dimensions.name: Colour palette
dimensions.description: How saturated and bright the colours are.

dimensions.name: Visual hierarchy
dimensions.description: How strongly one element stands out over the rest.

poles.name: Strong
poles.description: A clear focal point; clear steps between levels.

dimensions.name: Promotions
dimensions.description: The visual weight of promotional banners.

dimensions.name: Search entry
dimensions.description: How much the search box stands out.

poles.name: Prominent
poles.description: The search box is the visible main entry.

dimensions.name: Link affordance
dimensions.description: How links show that they are links.

dimensions.name: Imagery
dimensions.description: How much images lead the content cards.

poles.name: Image-led
poles.description: Images are prominent in cards and feed items.

poles.name: Collapsed
poles.description: Side content sits behind a Show button.

poles.name: Central
poles.description: Recommendations carry weight and sit closer to the top.

dimensions.name: Entry points
dimensions.description: Whether main destinations are repeated near the top.

poles.name: Surfaced
poles.description: A strip of shortcuts to existing destinations.
